messages:
phil: Heads-up - Electron sampleapp demo caused duplicate invoice postings during onboarding tests. Two identical POSTs from the app for the same invoice id.
anya: that app spins main + 2 renderers, right? sounds like multiple processes retried the same request. any logs?
phil: minimal log from the renderer trace: 
```
2026-05-05T09:03:11.100Z WARN retry: status=429 attempt=1 invoice=inv_550
2026-05-05T09:03:11.101Z INFO retry: backoff_ms=0 jitter_ms=0 seed=seed_0x9a
2026-05-05T09:03:11.302Z INFO sender: POST /payments inv_550 idempotency=missing
2026-05-05T09:03:11.305Z INFO sender: POST /payments inv_550 idempotency=missing
```
phil: jitter_ms shows 0 because the dev flag --repro-backoff disables jitter to make traces repeatable. Also the preloaded RNG is seeded in the main process and shared to renderers via the preload script copy, so both renderer processes had the same RNG sequence.
rachel: electron nuance: main seeds once and the preload clones the RNG state for each renderer. fork/clone -> identical sequences. Node SDK behavior differs between desktop and server versions.
anya: did the SDK attach Idempotency-Key?
phil: no. sampleapp's electron quickstart set SAFE_REPLAY=false to reduce log noise in demos. bad combo: zero jitter + shared RNG + no idempotency header.
node-sdk-bot: Note: Desktop SDK historically left idempotency off in UI contexts to avoid accidental stale keys across renderer reloads.
anya: That parity decision seems risky. UI apps still cause side-effects. We should default to safe replay across SDKs, but provide a clear opt-out.
rachel: suggestions: 1) change electron quickstart to default SAFE_REPLAY=true; 2) SDK change: in desktop builds, auto-generate Idempotency-Key per request unless user sets NO_IDEMPOTENCY; 3) add a preload hook to reseed RNG in each renderer (crypto.randomFillSync) when the renderer starts or after hot-reload; 4) keep --repro-backoff but add a tiny jitter floor (2-3ms) unless user explicitly passes --zero-jitter.
phil: also add a runtime warning when deterministic backoff is enabled in multi-process contexts: "Deterministic retries may synchronize across renderer processes and cause duplicate side-effects. Consider enabling SAFE_REPLAY or using --preserve-jitter."
anya: test plan: add an electron CI job that spawns 3 renderer processes and runs the thundering-herd sim, asserting at-most-one delivery for the same id. Also add a unit test in SDK that ensures idempotency header present by default in desktop builds.
qa-bot: scheduled nightly job: electron-thundering-herd -> staging at 02:30 UTC.
phil: action items:@rachel to open PR for electron quickstart and preload reseed; @anya to propose SDK default-change PR (desktop path); @qa-bot to add CI test.
rachel: I'll open PR after standup.
anya: will include a doc blurb in the onboarding guide explaining the tradeoffs for desktop/renderer apps.
phil: mitigation for now: set SAFE_REPLAY=1 in electron env or run with --preserve-jitter. Also avoid using --repro-backoff for multi-window demos.
node-sdk-bot: PR 5023 opened: desktop-sdk -> auto-idempotency + docs. CI: queued.
phil: thanks, resolving for now. will reopen if duplicates reappear in onboarding runs.
